reviewMethod: Independent visual sweep of all 32 paper pages and scheme pages 1–21. All printed tasks reconciled to the detailed mark boundaries, diagrams, contexts and answer requirements. Final question and solution crops inspected before publication.
sourceNotes: All ten offered questions retained: 48 tasks and 380 offered marks, despite the 220-mark candidate selection. Q6(a)(i–iii), Q9(c)(i–ii) and Q10(f)(i–ii) each share one published allocation and remain together.

Q1(b) requires De Moivre’s theorem: the scheme requires polar form for any credit and 0+5832i for its requested form. Q1(c) requires placement of all six numbers, not a finite choice; a labelled NextStepUni Venn example accompanies the original set-notation answer.

Q2(a)(ii) proves the odd-square statement for every odd number. Q2(a)(iii) is one induction proof; its P(1), P(k), P(k+1) steps are not separate questions. Non-negative integer witnesses m,h cover the case t=1.
Q2(b) has implicit domain restrictions x≠0 and x≠5/3. Q3(c) requires x≤7/11 or x>3/2; the pole is excluded.
Q4(b) asks for h(g(x)); the high-partial note about g(h(x)) is an alternative partial-credit condition, not the full-credit answer. Q5(c) uses k instead of x in the model working; x=ln4−ln7.
Q6(a) keeps local minimum (4,−29), maximum (0,3) and inflection (2,−13) on one 20D card. Q6(b)(ii) uses failure of injectivity; the source also lists mentioning surjectivity for partial credit.
Q7(a)(i) model table mislabels years 1–5. The paper uses years 0–4: €24000, €18000, €13500, €10125, €7593.75. An attributed corrected table retains the source below.

Q7(a)(iii) requires the first whole year below €1000: p=12. Q7(a)(iv) sums years 0–19, excluding year 20. Q7(b) uses the integral average, not the mean of two endpoints. Q7(d)(i) uses 300 monthly payments and monthly rate 0.0036.
Q8(a)(i) requires height and length; width already supplied. Q8(c) roots 0,15,21 refer to the polynomial, while the physical box requires 0<x<15. Q8(d) keeps the complete calculus proof together.

Q9(a)(i) correctly finds a=228 but prints V(x)=288x+2506 at the end. The corrected model is V(x)=228x+2506. Q9(a)(ii) supplies no worked quadratic; a labelled NextStepUni example V(x)=x²+227x+2506 and the complete family c≠0, d=228−c, f=2506 show all valid choices. These are open models, not separate cards.

Q9(c)(i–ii) share 5C. Display changes refer to rounding thresholds 47.5,115.5,116.5,117.5, not the displayed integers. Q9(c)(iv) retains the supplied equation and both requested results, x=36min and distance 246.75 km.

Q10(b) uses 201cm³ from part(a) in the source; retaining exact 64π gives the same height 5.80 cm to 2 dp. Q10(e) asks for radius-change rate but mistakenly prints cm³/s: correct units are cm/s, as in the scheme. dR/dt=−1/(4π)cm/s, so the radius decreases at 1/(4π)cm/s.
Q10(e) scheme lists any two intermediate steps for mid partial credit; that is examiner guidance, not a printed student choice. Q10(f)(i–ii) share 10C: slant height 4√10 cm and sector angle 114°.
